text:
Noah: hey team, weird onboarding edge-case. followed the Kandji invite on my new M2 MBP, but I also plugged in an external encrypted SSD (had Time Machine on it). now FileVault enrollment looks incomplete and Kandji shows "external protector detected". stuck on final escrow step. anyone seen an external disk interfere with FileVault/Mobile Device Management?
ivy-it: welcome Noah. interesting — external encrypted volumes can sometimes leave active personal protectors in the system keychain that block institutional escrow. did you enable FileVault during macOS setup or later?
Noah: during setup I picked company recovery, then later attached the SSD which had its own FileVault/backup encryption. I think Migration/Time Machine touched the local user home dir.
kate-kandji: Kandji here. we can see the device check-ins but the keyset shows a non-institutional protector present. Can you paste `sudo fdesetup status` and `diskutil apfs list`? small snippets are ok.
Noah: pasted outputs:
```bash
$ sudo fdesetup status
FileVault is On.
Users: Noah (Enabled)
Escrow: Partial - non-institutional protectors present
```
```bash
$ diskutil apfs list
... Volume disk2s1 (External)... Encrypted: Yes
... Volume disk1s1 (Internal)... Encrypted: Yes (FileVault)
```
ivy-it: thanks. that confirms an external APFS encrypted volume is attached. Kandji's escrow agent doesn't grab institutional key when non-institutional protectors exist. Two safe routes: 1) detach the external SSD and we force a keyset push (fast), 2) we open a temp-admin and remove the external protector entry manually, then escrow (fast but logged), 3) re-enroll with a clean boot (slow). Which do you prefer?
Noah: I can unplug the SSD now. prefer the non-admin unplug route if that fixes it.
mdm-bot: Kandji last check-in: 2026-03-10T10:05:32Z. Device status: Enrolled. FileVault escrow: Partial. Pending: push-escrow-after-detach.
ivy-it: unplug the external, wait 30s, then run `sudo fdesetup refresh` and ping me the output. I'll also monitor Kandji for the push.
Noah: unplugged SSD and ran refresh. output:
```bash
$ sudo fdesetup refresh
Refreshing FileVault status...
Escrow: Institutional recovery key pending
```
Noah: Kandji UI now shows "escrow in progress".
kate-kandji: we've received the request. pushing institutional keyset now. will verify with the device once it checks in.
Noah: running `sudo fdesetup status` again after a minute shows:
```bash
$ sudo fdesetup status
FileVault is On.
Users: Noah (Enabled)
Escrow: Institutional recovery key present (Kandji)
```
Noah: restarting to confirm unlock flow.
Noah: restart done. FileVault accepted my login password and no errors. :thumbsup:
ivy-it: great. two notes: 1) if you plan to keep that external encrypted disk, avoid connecting it until after MDM checks are complete during initial enroll; 2) if the SSD contains company backups we recommend migrating them to the managed backup target so we control recovery keys.
alex-sec: security ack. recorded the operation and verified escrow is present. if Noah needs to re-add the external SSD, we'll coordinate a documented flow that clears any conflicting protectors first.
rachel-people: logged this in onboarding ticket #ONB-5345 and adding a quick tip to the new-hire doc about "unplug external encrypted drives during first boot/enrollment".
Noah: thanks everyone — that was painless. will keep the SSD unplugged next time.
